title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.62, Prop. 2.4 of the notes). X is smooth projective of dimension n over k, and Y is a smooth projective variety, in effect a curve or something with an interesting H^1. β is a correspondence on X×Y. It induces a(γ(β)): H^1(Y,Q_ℓ) → H^{2n-1}(X,Q_ℓ)(n-1). A_Y and B_X are the abelian varieties attached to Y and X (Picard and Albanese type). Through the identifications H^1(Y) ≅ H^1(A_Y) and H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1) ≅ H^1(B_X), the map a(γ(β)) becomes u^{(ℓ)}, the ℓ-adic realisation of a homomorphism u of abelian varieties.

The page argues as follows, with ℓ prime to the characteristic.
(i) a(γ(β)) is an isomorphism iff u^{(ℓ)} is, i.e. iff u is an isogeny. This uses that T_ℓ and V_ℓ detect isogenies.
(ii) If so, u has a unique inverse in Hom(A_Y,B_X)⊗Q, a quasi-homomorphism. By Weil's theory of divisorial correspondences, homomorphisms between Picard and Albanese varieties are exactly those induced by divisor classes on X×Y. So the inverse of a(γ(β)) is induced by a Q-divisor D, with the best possible denominator R. This is the 'first assertion'.
(iii) The 'second assertion' concerns the denominator: D can be taken of the form N^{-r}D_0 with D_0 integral, and the best denominator is a power of N. For ℓ ≠ p this is read off from the degree of the isogeny u. For p = char k it is deduced from how the corresponding datum on isocrystals (Dieudonné modules) acts on the abelian varieties. A reference is left blank ('cf ...').
(iv) It remains to see that a denominator valid for D is valid for the Q-homomorphism inverse to u. That inverse can be no better than a power of N.

The page then begins Corollary 2.5. The next page gives the integral criterion: the composite of H^1(Y,Z_ℓ) → H^{2n-1}(X,Z_ℓ)(n-1) with passage to H^{2n-1} modulo torsion is bijective iff ℓ is prime to N. Corollary 2.6 follows: for X with ample classes ξ_1,…,ξ_{n-1}, cup product with η = ξ_1⋯ξ_{n-1} gives H^1 ≅ H^{2n-1}(n-1). Its inverse Λ is induced by a unique Q-divisor class on X×X, independent of ℓ. This is the Lefschetz standard conjecture B in degree 1 ('Lefschetz vectoriel').
errors: Logic and argument are sound; the remaining gaps are expository rather than mathematical.

The step 'the inverse quasi-isogeny is induced by a Q-divisorial correspondence' relies on the bijection between Hom(Alb, Pic^0) and divisorial correspondences modulo trivial ones. This is not restated here.
The p-part (isocrystal) argument is only gestured at, with an empty 'cf ...' reference.
The text is self-correcting (the phrase 'prouve la première assertion' appears twice), so it is a draft. The relation between N and the degree of u is not made explicit on this page.

ideas.what: A correspondence induces an isomorphism H^1(Y) → H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1) iff the associated homomorphism of abelian varieties is an isogeny; the inverse is then algebraic, given by a Q-divisor on X×Y.
ideas.modern_name: Algebraicity of inverses of isogenies via divisorial correspondences; standard conjecture B in degree 1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil (correspondence theory); Grothendieck, Kleiman (1968) and Lieberman for Lefschetz-type conjectures in degree ≤1
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1968/69) mentions the low-degree cases; details in Kleiman, 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: Integral refinement: the denominator of the inverse correspondence is a power of N, the primes dividing the isogeny degree, and is best possible. Hence an integral Lefschetz-type isomorphism holds for Z_ℓ exactly when ℓ is prime to N (modulo torsion).
ideas.modern_name: Integral or ℓ-adic Lefschetz for H^1; degree of the polarisation isogeny Pic^0 → Alb
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; implicit in the theory of polarisations and in later integral-Lefschetz discussions

ideas.what: Using isocrystals and Dieudonné theory to control the p-part of denominators of algebraic correspondences in characteristic p.
ideas.modern_name: Crystalline Dieudonné theory; p-adic realisation of homomorphisms of abelian varieties
ideas.where_published: Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné (Montréal 1970); letter to Tate 1966 (circulated)

missed.claim: Grothendieck intends to handle the p-primary part of the denominator of the Lefschetz inverse via the 'effet arithmétique' of isocrystal data, but leaves the reference empty. It is a small, explicit marker of crystalline methods being planned for the integral and p-adic standard conjecture B in degree 1.
missed.quote: la seconde résulte de la connaissance de l'effet arithmétique d'une donnée corr. d'isocristaux, via l'effet sur les VA ... (cf ... )
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is mostly of historical interest: the p-adic and integral versions of Lefschetz for H^1 follow from Dieudonné theory, which is standard today.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine proof step of the degree-1 Lefschetz standard conjecture, which is known and published (Kleiman 1968). The integral/denominator refinement and the mention of isocrystals for the p-part are minor unpublished details, not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'α(T(B)) soit un Dom' should read 'a(γ(β)) soit un isom'.
Header: likely '(ℓ étant donné premier à car k)', i.e. the characteristic, not 'card'.

'Il reste : [-prouver-] nateur' is better read as 'Il reste à voir que si D admet un certain dénominateur, ce dernier vaut pour le Q-hom A_Y → B_X inverse de u, lequel ne peut être meilleur que puissance de N'.
The inserted phrase reads roughly 'ayant même dénominateur que R'.
